name: Sirolimus
route_note: oral tablets or solution once daily; albumin-bound IV infusion for PEComa; topical gel for facial angiofibroma
originator: Ayerst Laboratories (Suren Sehgal); developed by Wyeth

discovery.by: Suren Sehgal and colleagues, Ayerst Research Laboratories
discovery.note: Isolated from Streptomyces hygroscopicus in soil collected on Easter Island (Rapa Nui) in 1964; first studied as an antifungal.

tagline: Easter Island macrolide that founded mTOR biology
summary: Sirolimus, also called rapamycin, is a macrolide from an Easter Island soil bacterium that inhibits the kinase mTOR. It prevents kidney transplant rejection, treats lymphangioleiomyomatosis, and is used on drug-eluting stents. Studies of its mechanism led to the discovery of the mTOR growth-signalling pathway.
mechanism: Sirolimus binds FKBP12, and the complex binds the FRB domain of mTOR, inhibiting mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1). mTORC1 integrates growth-factor and nutrient signals to drive protein synthesis and cell-cycle progression.

In T cells, blocking mTORC1 stops interleukin-2-driven progression from G1 to S phase, so unlike calcineurin inhibitors it acts downstream of cytokine production. Antiproliferative effects on smooth muscle and tumour cells underlie its use in stents, lymphangioleiomyomatosis and PEComa.
uses: Malignant perivascular epithelioid cell tumour (PEComa, nab-sirolimus)
Facial angiofibroma in tuberous sclerosis complex (topical)

history.title: Isolation
history.detail: Rapamycin is isolated at Ayerst from an Easter Island soil sample.

history.title: Revival
history.detail: After the project was shelved, Sehgal's preserved cultures allow renewed study as an immunosuppressant.

history.title: mTOR identified
history.detail: Several groups identify the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) as its molecular target.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Rapamune approved for prophylaxis of kidney transplant rejection.

history.title: Drug-eluting stent
history.detail: The sirolimus-eluting Cypher coronary stent is approved in the US.

history.title: LAM approval
history.detail: FDA approves sirolimus for lymphangioleiomyomatosis after the MILES trial.

history.title: Fyarro
history.detail: Albumin-bound sirolimus approved for advanced malignant PEComa.

history.title: Topical gel
history.detail: Hyftor approved for facial angiofibroma in tuberous sclerosis complex.

serious: hepatic artery thrombosis after liver transplantation
bronchial anastomotic dehiscence after lung transplantation
safety.boxed_warning: Increased susceptibility to infection and possible lymphoma; not recommended in liver transplantation (hepatic artery thrombosis, graft loss and death) or lung transplantation (bronchial anastomotic dehiscence).

facts: Rapamycin extends lifespan in mice and other model organisms, making it a central compound in ageing research.
